claims.text: Introducing chemically controlled SRO precipitates into an electrically insulating, high-purity ceramic matrix will reduce lattice thermal conductivity relative to the pristine material.
Doped or stabilized zirconia is a suitable example of the proposed ceramic matrix.
Heat in the proposed electrically insulating, high-purity ceramic is largely carried by phonons, with minimal electronic conduction.
Controlled doping and thermal processing can introduce SRO precipitates into the ceramic.
At moderate to high temperatures, lattice transport dominates and electronic contributions are negligible in the proposed material.
The proposed processing produces SRO precipitates within the ceramic matrix.
SRO precipitates act as phonon-scattering centers.
Scattering by SRO precipitates reduces phonon mean free paths or scattering times.
Reducing phonon mean free paths or scattering times lowers lattice thermal conductivity.
A ceramic containing engineered SRO precipitates will exhibit a measurable decrease in thermal conductivity compared with a pristine control.
A homogeneous dopant distribution with minimal local ordering provides a baseline without controlled SRO precipitates.
The conductivity reduction depends on precipitate size, spacing, and volume fraction being in a range that effectively scatters phonons.
Temperatures outside the phonon-dominated transport regime may obscure the effect of SRO precipitates.
Laser-flash analysis or time-domain thermoreflectance can be used to measure the relevant thermal conductivity.
TEM or XRD can confirm the presence and distribution of the proposed SRO precipitates.
